transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. It is very likely broken. Running a microwave empty for 10 minutes sends all the energy into the magnetron and other internal components instead of heating food, which often causes parts to overheat, melt, or burn out. Because there is an active burning smell, you must stop using it immediately. Do not try to run it again to test if it works; this could cause a fire or further damage that makes repair impossible. The smell suggests something inside has melted or scorched (often the waveguide cover or internal wiring). Please unplug the appliance and arrange for a qualified engineer to inspect it before use.

candidates: Internal damage from dry running (magnetron, HV capacitor, or waveguide cover) (high)

reading.symptom: horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
